LESSON: MUSICAL SOUNDS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Creating and Execution
Topic 1.2: Musical Sounds
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Musical Sounds, part of Creating and Execution in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one CREATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How do we sense sounds and sound vibrations? 2. How can we makes objects to produce sounds?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Musical Sounds together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Communication and collaboration: Listening/Observing; as the learner listens attentively to sounds or observes keenly in order to sense and

on how sounds is produced from different sources and how they are sensed differently for perception.

Creativity and imagination: Communication and self-expression; as the learner confidently expresses self by imitating sounds and

demonstrate how the birds, animals and other objects behave when producing sounds in their environment.

Digital literacy: Interaction with digital technology; as the learner interacts with ICT devices while recording imitated sounds and movements

of birds, animals and objects using ICT devices.

Values:
Responsibility: Accountability; as the learner cares for own costumes and props when performing songs.

Respect: Acceptance; as the learner appreciates peers’ imitations of the identified sounds or visual cues of birds, animals and objects.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety and security: Personal safety; as the learner observers own and others safety during singing.

Link to other learning areas.

• English, Kiswahili, and Indigenous Languages Activities: as the learner expresses self by imitating the identified sounds of birds, animals

and objects.

7

• Environmental Activities: as the learner applies knowledge gained in Environmental Activities to role play, imitate and identify sounds of

various birds, animals and objects.

Suggested learning resources:

Open safe quiet space, digital devices: laptops, tablets, phones, computers, chime bars, drums, shakers, whistles, horns, flutes, vuvuzelas,

flash cards, picture tags, glue, manila paper, papier mache, feathers, cotton wool, tuning forks, sisal fibers, colours. reference books
